g.text: $ ./airprint-doctor
airprint-doctor 1.0.0 · macOS 27.2 · CUPS 2.3.4
Looking for printers on the network (5s)...
Found 1 printer(s) on the network.
✗ Offline: the printer renamed itself and this queue still looks for the old name
Queue looks for: "Canon MF645C (1a:2b:3c) (1a:2b:3c) (1a:2b:3c)"
Printer is now: "Canon MF645C (1a:2b:3c) (1a:2b:3c)"
Fix: point the queue at the printer's host name instead: ipps://Canon1a2b3c.local:10443/ipp/print
✓ The printer answers and reports no errors
✗ Paper list is broken: this Mac only offers Letter
When macOS added the printer it couldn't read the printer's paper list, so it
fell back to US Letter only. Letter jobs on A4 paper make many printers stop
and ask for paper.
Fix: the printer answers cleanly now (19 paper sizes), so the list can be rebuilt.
! This Mac shares the printer again, so phones and other computers see it twice
The copy that goes through this Mac stops working whenever the Mac sleeps.
Fix: stop sharing it from this Mac. The printer still shows up on its own.
✗ Queue is paused on this Mac
macOS pauses a queue after a printing error and leaves it paused.
Fix: resume it.
! The printer's own network name carries clash tags: "Canon MF645C (1a:2b:3c) (1a:2b:3c)"
Rename it to "Canon MF645C" on the printer's web page (http://Canon1a2b3c.local),
usually under Network › Bonjour (mDNS) or AirPrint. It can't be done from the Mac.
It renames itself when it drops off the network and comes back while its
old name is still remembered. A cable, a stronger Wi-Fi spot or a reserved
address on the router makes this rarer.
! Default printer is "Last Printer Used", which changes with the network
macOS remembers one printer per network it has been on. After a router
change, prints can quietly go to a different printer than you expect.
It still remembers 1 printer(s) you no longer have:
Old_Office_HP
Fix: pick one fixed default printer.
6 problem(s) found. To repair them, run: airprint-doctor --fix
Each change asks first, and --undo puts things back.
